_comment: Settings for scripts/collect_water.py (Market page, tab 'Water'). 'gauges': river gauges from PEGELONLINE (Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration, free API, licence DL-DE->Zero-2.0); 'station' is the PEGELONLINE short name, 'match' is used when the short name is not found (part of the long name). Characteristic values (GlW, MNW, MW) come from PEGELONLINE itself; 'thresholds' adds your own lines (e.g. where barge low-water surcharges start in WEPA's contracts). 'sites': WEPA mills in Germany (public addresses); the collector picks the nearest DWD station that has daily soil-moisture data (Deutscher Wetterdienst, CC BY 4.0). Only public data, nothing internal.

gauges.label: Rhine · Kaub
gauges.why: The bottleneck gauge for Rhine barges. Low water means lighter loads, surcharges and slower deliveries of pulp, recovered paper and chemicals.

thresholds.label: Low-water surcharges usually start (adjust to our contracts)

gauges.label: Rhine · Mainz
gauges.why: Gauge next to the Mainz mill: river level for water intake, cooling and logistics.

gauges.label: Saale · Leuna-Kreypau
gauges.why: Gauge next to the Leuna mill.

soil._comment: Soil moisture in % of usable field capacity (nFK), 0-60 cm under grass. Below 50 % plants start to suffer, below 30 % is drought stress (DWD/agronomy convention). The first matching column is used.
